_meta.title: Chinese star names with their modern identifications
_meta.scope: The 312 traditional asterisms of the three enclosures and the twenty-eight lunar lodges, together with the individual stars and deep-sky objects that names in the record corpus point to. The stars added by the Qing survey of 1752 are not collected, since no earlier text names them, nor are stars that carry no Chinese name. Field allocations, character conversion tables and the question of whether a name denotes a region or a single star are all outside this table.
_meta.fields: key = standard name in Simplified Chinese. hant = the same name in Traditional Chinese. kind = lodge, enclosure, officer, star or cluster. in = the asterism this entry belongs to. rom = romanisation. en/fr/es/it/ja = the sense of the name. alias = older, variant and alternative written forms. modern = the modern identification, either {hip, bf, proper, mag, con, ra, dec} for a star or {designation, ...} for other objects. src = whether the entry is machine-derived or established by hand.
_meta.provenance: Asterism names, the European-language readings and the star identifications are drawn from the sky data of the companion project AstroMeteoMap, which in turn rests on Wikipedia, HYG and SIMBAD. Entries added by hand are marked as such. The Japanese column is derived by converting the Traditional Chinese name to present-day Japanese character forms, Japanese astronomy having kept the Chinese asterism names and only written them in its own forms. The planet section is original to this project. The Huihui star table of Yabuuchi Kiyoshi (1964) was consulted offline for comparison only, and none of its data is reproduced here. modern.ra/dec are J2000 equatorial coordinates in degrees without proper motion, since over five millennia the proper motion of a naked-eye star stays far below the precision at which a lodge boundary can be read from a text.
caveats: Five hant forms are corrected by hand where an automatic conversion from Simplified Chinese picked the wrong variant: 斗 (given as 鬥, to fight), 小斗, 东咸 and 西咸 (given as 鹹, salty), and 卷舌 (given as 捲, to roll up). The wrong forms are kept as aliases, because historical texts as transcribed carry them and a lookup on the received form has to keep working.

Unresolved: the forms 鬥 and 鹹 in the transcribed texts belong to the edition rather than to the original source. Fifty-one passages resolve through 鬥 to the asterism 斗 of the Heavenly Market enclosure, which the English reading renders as the Dipper for Liquids while the Chinese reading treats it as the lodge 斗. The two languages disagree and the case is open.
Asterisms that share a name, among them 三公, 积尸, 天田, 杵, 钺 and 柱, are distinguished by the enclosure or lodge they sit in. The key keeps that qualifier and it cannot be stripped.

The Beehive cluster (M44, Praesepe) has no entry of its own. It is carried as an alias and modern identification of the asterism 积尸 in the lodge 鬼, the two being ancient and modern names for one object.
天籥, 斗, 權 and 水位 are entries in their own right even though a text may use any of them for the lodge or neighbouring asterism it belongs to.
